audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven chart rows disagrees with its own why. The file marks Level 1 Skill while its why and early[] both say 'Level 1 is genuinely his'; it marks Levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items for Renekton while their whys say Maokai out-trades, out-grinds and out-lasts him; and it marks Levels 4-5 and 6 Skill while their whys call the lane 'already-favored' for Maokai.
audit.why: Renekton's power is a Fury-empowered point-and-click stun with no cooldown cost, which beats a one-ability Maokai at Level 1. From Level 2 Twisted Advance into Bramble Smash is a trade he cannot repeat because Fury has to be rebuilt, and Sap Magic refunds Cull the Meek's chip. Renekton has no item scaling; Maokai's damage also flattens, so 2+ items is a genuine standoff.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Renekton / Maokai / Maokai / Maokai / Maokai / Maokai / Skill in both layers — the packet chart — with matching ratings, and difficulty relabelled EVEN at 6/10 to match the 54.08% win rate.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly ordered as Lvl 1 (his), Lvl 2-3 (the takeover), Lvl 6 (modest bump), 1st item (yours). The chart should have matched this all along.

audit.whatIsWrong: The file repeatedly says 'empowered = long stun' and 'don't trade into full fury' without a single number, and never mentions that the empowered cast also destroys damage shields. dontsFull[0] and dontsFull[1] both carry descriptions unrelated to their titles.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator stuns 0.75s normally and 1.5s above 50 Fury — double, and the difference between surviving a trade and eating a full combo. The empowered cast additionally destroys damage shields on the target, which quietly deletes shield value Maokai builds toward. Cooldown is 16/14/12/10/8s, so at rank 1 a spent W is a 16-second window.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now gives both stun durations and the 16s cooldown; dontsFull[0].d states the 50-Fury threshold scaling both his heal and his stun; dontsFull[1].d states the shield destruction.
sources: champ-data/_kits/renekton.json (W text and cooldown, Q text)

audit.whatIsWrong: Maokai's kit file gives Bramble Smash a 'grounding — shuts off enemy dashes' flag. Against Renekton that would read as a hard answer to Slice and Dice, and it would be wrong to write it.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Bramble Smash is 'knocks back nearby enemies with a shockwave, dealing magic damage and slowing them' — no grounding component. Per the standing rule that the description outranks a derived flag, I did not assert grounding anywhere in this matchup, and no advice here depends on it.
audit.corrected: No edit made — recorded so a later pass does not 'add the missing grounding interaction'.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Renekton contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Empowered Ruthless Predator point-click stuns you and Cull the Meek heals the chip — you have one ability and no answer.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Renekton's Ruthless Predator is down.
edits.after: Your Level 2 W into Q gives you a root-and-knockback trade his Fury cannot repeat, and Sap Magic heals the whole thing back.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Renekton must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: W, Q and E let you repeat root trades around his Fury while Sap Magic grinds straight through Cull the Meek's heal.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ruthless Predator's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your root cooldowns and constant Sap Magic healing win the attrition war his point-click bully kit cannot sustain through 4-5.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Renekton's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp adds a long-range root for ganks and all-in threat on top of an already favoured lane — a bump, not a takeover.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Ruthless Predator's cooldown.
edits.after: Your first sustain item makes his Fury combo trade unevenly while Sap Magic heals the chip.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Renekton carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He falls off hard into items but your own damage flattens too — neither solo-kills, so your edge is pure teamfight utility.

edits.before: Empowered = long stun. Root/bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Empowered is a 1.5s stun, plain is 0.75s; 16s at rank 1. Bait it first.

edits.before: That is Renekton's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Above 50 Fury his Q heal and W stun both scale up — trade at an empty bar.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Empowered W also destroys your shields — bait his Fury bar down first.

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. Survive his Level 1 window, then every stage from Level 2 onward is yours until the game flattens.
